activation_routing.verdict: keyword-explicit only: the user must say 'team mode' (or the model decides once the tools exist); there is NO complexity/size heuristic and NO session-start auto-provisioning
activation_routing.trigger_action: keyword detector (Transform tier on messages.transform) scans the FIRST user message and injects the [team-mode] prompt: 'Orchestrate via team_* tools … NEVER substitute with delegate_task'
activation_routing.second_surface: team-mode-status-injector re-checks the LATEST real user message each turn and injects <team_mode_status enabled="true"> plus the closure invariant
activation_routing.no_auto_mode: packages/omo-opencode/src/config/schema/default-mode.ts declares exactly TWO auto-injection switches — ultrawork (auto-inject ulw prompt) and goal (auto-create a goal). There is deliberately no default_mode.team: team mode is never auto-started.
activation_routing.scoping: the team keyword is filtered out in non-main sessions (index.test.ts 'should filter team-mode keyword in non-main session (only ultrawork allowed there)')

eligibility.verdict: three verdict tiers; read-only specialists are HARD-REJECTED as team members

citations.quote: ELIGIBLE AGENTS — eligible: sisyphus, atlas, sisyphus-junior; conditional: hephaestus; hard-reject: oracle, librarian, explore, multimodal-looker, metis, momus, prometheus (read-only or plan-mode-only)
The curated agents are read-only and in-process, so they can't write mailbox state. Route both groups through the task tool instead.

lifecycle_and_closure.verdict: explicit closure contract: the lead must shut down and delete the team in the same turn once every task is terminal; lingering teams are a defect

citations.quote: Closure invariant: every team you open is yours to close … if every task is terminal, run team_shutdown_request + team_approve_shutdown per active member, then team_delete — in the same turn … Lingering teams are a defect.
Closing the team is the lead's responsibility, not the user's.

repo_mechanism.verdict: the OPPOSITE default: every qualifying mpd session is mechanically provisioned into a staged 'MPD Default' team at its first agent/pre-step, with no keyword, no size judgment and no user opt-in
repo_mechanism.config_source: bundle patch row config only (packages/mpd-bundle/cordis.patch.yml) + the legacy installer mirror; the .mpd/mpd.jsonc config plane does NOT expose sessionTeamPolicy
repo_mechanism.qualification: non-child session (header.parentSession absent) AND (no preset OR preset in ['mpd']); settles once per agent id (no recreation after delete)
repo_mechanism.provisioning_path: same as the agent_teams_create(approval=required, profile=...) tool (initializeProfileTeam, staged) — the 11-member mpd roster is written as roster rows; nothing spawns until the user approves the Web plan
repo_mechanism.no_closure: there is no shutdown/delete path for the auto-provisioned default team: it persists until the user deletes it, and the policy never recreates it

measured_residue.what: auto-provisioned default teams left in this workspace by the always-on policy

breakdown.note: pure residue — provisioned, never used, never cleaned

measured_residue.interpretation: an always-on provision with no closure produces unbounded per-session state that nothing ever reclaims; upstream's off-by-default + explicit closure invariant is the structural counterexample

open_questions_for_requirements: t1 must freeze the target default: pure OMO parity (mode off, tools present, model/user decides), instruct-only (notice, no auto-create), or triggered-auto (auto-provision only for tasks meeting a size/complexity rule).

If complex tasks must auto-route mechanically, what is the signal? OMO has NO complexity heuristic to port — candidates: keyword surface (team mode / ulw / agent-teams), the persona's small/large judgment, or a task-size threshold defined by t1. This is the one genuine design decision, not a parity question.
Should the policy live in a config plane (.mpd/mpd.jsonc via mpd-config-plugin) like upstream's team_mode, or stay a bundle-patch constant? t5's brief names a '配置平面'.
Does the always-on usageSectionText/captainPrompt need weakening when the policy is off, or does the manual /agent-teams entry keep it?
Should the 25 residual .mpd/team/mpd-default* directories be reclaimed as part of this work (they are workspace state, not evidence)?
out_of_scope_observations: Skills corpus references to 'team mode' (skills/ulw-research/SKILL.md:62, skills/debugging, skills/refactor) are adopted upstream texts that already phrase team mode as conditional ('when your harness gives you it') — they are not asserting mpd's auto policy. Corpus-level decisions belong to t2/t4/t8/t9.
Upstream 'team_mode' and upstream 'ultrawork/workflow/mass-ulw' are separate subsystems; this file covers only enablement/routing. The workflow/mass-ulw semantics comparison is t2's deliverable.
